children: South Africa chemicals and energy firm's FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 17% on improved operations
FY26 basic EPS up 79% and headline EPS up 9% from prior year
Net debt fell 11% to US$3.3 bln, still above threshold for dividend resumption
Sasol aims to reduce net debt to sustainably below US$3 bln before resuming dividends
Company says improving working capital is a key priority for strengthening cash conversion
Sasol will use higher year-end fuels inventory to support planned shutdowns early in 2027
OPERATIONAL IMPROVEMENTS - Co said improved production and higher equipment availability boosted sales volumes by 4%
COST CONTAINMENT - Sasol maintained cash fixed costs flat for the third year, citing continued cost optimisation initiatives
MARKET TAILWINDS - Higher Brent crude oil prices and refining margins in Q4 supported earnings, though partially offset by a stronger Rand/US$ exchange rate
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "hold" and the breakdown of recommendations is 3 "strong buy" or "buy", 6 "hold" and 1 "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the diversified chemicals peer group is "buy."
The stock recently traded at 5 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 6 three months ago
